key_insight: CorDex can synthesize diverse, functional dexterous grasps for novel objects from a single human demonstration by combining semantic affordance reasoning with geometry-aware contact generation and transfer/adaptation to a robot hand.
problem_solved: Overcomes the twin bottlenecks of limited large-scale dexterous grasp data and the lack of integrated semantic + geometric reasoning, enabling functional tool-use grasps from minimal human input.
method: Generate: create a large synthetic grasp dataset by perturbing and augmenting one human demonstration guided by object affordances and semantic labels.
Transfer: retarget human-hand grasps to a dexterous robotic hand using kinematic mapping and contact-aware optimization to preserve functional contacts.
Adapt: refine and filter candidate grasps with physics-based simulation and sim-to-real adaptation (domain randomization / fine-tuning) to ensure robust execution.
impact: Enables fast bootstrapping of functional dexterous manipulation for new objects with minimal human effort, reducing data collection and accelerating deployment of robot tool-use in real-world tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single human demo -> synthetic grasp generation -> retargeting -> adaptation -> robot execution
Before/After visuals: image of human demonstration next to corresponding robot hand grasp on novel objects
Affordance & contact maps: object overlay showing semantic affordances and predicted contact points
Performance chart: success rates (sim and real) comparing CorDex to baselines or ablations
paper_title: Generate, Transfer, Adapt: Learning Functional Dexterous Grasping from a Single Human Demonstration
paper_authors: Xingyi He, Adhitya Polavaram, Yunhao Cao, Om Deshmukh, Tianrui Wang
